To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

perturbative factorization theorem for $\Lambda_b \rightarrow \Lambda_c$ decay is applicable for velocity transfer $v>1.2$ and that the branching ratio $ B(\Lambda_b\to\Lambda_c l\overline{\nu})\simeq 2\%$.

perturbative factorization is applicable for $\Lambda_b \rightarrow \Lambda_c l {\bar\nu}$ decays, with branching ratio of $B(\Lambda_{b}\rightarrow\Lambda_{c}l{\bar\nu}\sim2\%)$, and that the $\Lambda_b$, $\Lambda_c$ wave functions can be determined.
we develop perturbative quantum chromodynamics factorization theorem for $\Lambda_b \rightarrow \Lambda_c$ baysronic decays, which renders the perturbative expansion more reliable.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the perturbative QED factorization theorem for semileptonic $\Lambda_b \rightarrow \Lambda_c$ transitions.
the application of the perturbative QED to the semileptotic decay of the Lambda(b) baryon to the Lambda(c) baryon.
the perturbative QED factorization theorem for heavy baryon semileptonic decays, and the application of perturbative methods to $\Lambda_b$ decays.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the perturbative Qcd is not applicable to Lambda b ---> Lambda c decays.
perturbative calculations of $\Lambda_b \rightarrow \Lambda_c l {\bar\nu}$ decay are reliable for $q^2 > 1.2$.
perturbative theory of heavy quark decay, with the inclusion of the Sudakov resummed corrections, is applicable to $\bar B \to \bar D$ and $\Lambda_b \rightarrow \Lambda_c$ semileptonic decays.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the heavy quark effective theory and perturbative Q.C.D. are applicable to heavy baryon decays, and can provide useful information for the baryon wave function and the form factors.
the perturbative QED and QCD are both reliable to describe the heavy baryon decays.
perturbative factorization is applicable to heavy baryon decays as well as heavy meson decays.
The main takeaway from our work is that
perturbative calculations of heavy baryon form factors are feasible.
the perturbative QFT factorization is applicable to the $\Lambda_b \rightarrow \Lambda_c$ transition.
perturbative factorization is valid for $\Lambda_b \rightarrow \Lambda_c$ decay, which can be used to test heavy quark symmetry.
